**Filed the two path contributions from the PR #360 review as comments on #316 and #284**

**What**: Posted the two additive findings from the PR #360 reviewer session as comments on existing open tickets, deliberately NOT as new issues.
- #316 (unify .env parsers): https://github.com/csrinaldi/brain/issues/316#issuecomment-5120918911 — reports `brain/scripts/review/identity.mjs:34` as a missing 5th call site (reads `process.env` only) versus `vcs/lib/token.mjs:26-34` (reads `.env` then falls back), plus the `docs/reviewer-setup.md:12-13` knock-on. Asks that the doc be corrected in the same slice that lands `readEnv()`.
- #284 (reviewer v2): https://github.com/csrinaldi/brain/issues/284#issuecomment-5120919263 — PR #360 as evidence that deferred item 3's opening criterion is one-directional (cost/skip only) and should also cover risk-escalation. States explicitly that the tranche `APPROVE` is spec-correct per REQ-H1-8, so the comment is not misread as a bug report against the evaluator.

**Why**: Owner ruled that every discovery must be re-verified against epic #313 and its nested tickets before being treated as a finding. That check showed most of the session's "findings" were already ticketed (#317, #284) or were my own error (see [[review/brain-review-tranche-doctrine-blindspot]]). Only these two were additive, and both extend open tickets rather than warranting new ones.

**Where**: GitHub issues #316, #284. Comment bodies drafted under the session scratchpad. Written in English per brain.config.json `docs.language: en`, following the `comment-writer` skill.

**Learned**: Contributing to an existing ticket's inventory or opening criteria is the correct output when a discovery lands inside already-scheduled work. Filing a new issue there would have fragmented the path.
